name: Quatre Sept
description: Quatre Sept is a French-Canadian four-player partnership point-trick game with no trumps, descended from Italian Tressette. Players use a 32-card pack (10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7). Holding all four sevens wins the game immediately; winning three consecutive tricks with 10-9-A of a suit (La Politaine) scores an 11-point bonus.

overview.description: Quatre Sept is a French-Canadian four-player partnership point-trick game with no trumps, descended from Italian Tressette. Players use a 32-card pack (10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7). Holding all four sevens wins the game immediately; winning three consecutive tricks with 10-9-A of a suit (La Politaine) scores an 11-point bonus.

history.origins: Quatre Sept is played in the French-speaking provinces of Canada. It descends from the Italian game Tressette, which was fashionable throughout Europe in the 18th century. French players adapted Tressette to the 32-card pack (no 3 or 2), substituting 10 and 9 for those ranks. The game was exported to Canada with the ranking 10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7.
timeline: 18th century: Tressette fashionable in Europe; 18th-century French/German sources mention three- and four-sevens bonuses.
19th century: Tressette's sevens bonuses abandoned in Europe but survived in the Canadian variant.
French adaptation: 32-card pack adopted; ranking 10-9-A-K-Q-J-8-7; Trois Sept â†’ Quatre Sept.
Canadian development: Four sevens in hand = instant game win; La Politaine (Napolitane) bonus retained.
Present: Played in Quebec and other French-Canadian regions.
history.cultural: A staple of French-Canadian card play. The alternative name La Poule may derive from La Politaine. Related German variant Pollack (19th century) uses similar scoring with declaration bonuses.
history.evolution: Tressette (three sevens) became Trois Sept in France; the Canadian variant added the four-sevens instant win and was named Quatre Sept. La Politaine (from Italian Napolitaneâ€”10-9-A of a suit) gives an 11-point bonus when used to win three consecutive tricks.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships. Partners sit opposite each other.
setup.deck: 32-card French pack: 10, 9, A, K, Q, J, 8, 7 in each suit. No trumps.
setup.dealing: 1. Deal 8 cards each in batches of 3-2-3. 2. Deal and play clockwise. 3. If any player has all four sevens, that team wins the game immediately.

rules.objective: Win tricks to score points. First team to reach 31 or more wins. Four sevens in hand wins the game instantly. La Politaine (10-9-A of a suit) used to win three consecutive tricks scores an 11-point bonus.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Lead**: Player to dealer's left leads. Winner of each trick leads the next. 2. **Play**: Any card may be led. Must follow suit if possible; if void, may play any card. No trumpsâ€”highest card of the suit led wins. 3. **La Politaine**: If a player holds 10-9-A of a suit and wins three consecutive tricks with them, announce before playing the first card; team scores 11-point bonus. 4. **Scoring**: At end of hand, count points: Aces 1 each; 10,9,K,Q,J 1/3 each; 8,7 nothing; last trick 1. Fractional points ignored; total 11 per hand. 5. **Winning**: First team to 31+ wins. Tie at 33: play another deal.
keyRules: No trumps. Highest card of the suit led wins the trick.
Four sevens in one hand = immediate game win for that team.
La Politaine: 10-9-A of a suit; must announce before first play; must win three consecutive tricks with those cards to score 11-point bonus.
Card values: A=1; 10,9,K,Q,J=1/3 each; 8,7=0. Last trick=1.

strategy.basic: Lead from your long suits to pull cards. Save high cards to win point-bearing tricks. If you have La Politaine, try to obtain the lead and win three tricks in a row with 10-9-A.
strategy.intermediate: Count points in tricks to know when you have enough. Signal partner (e.g. tap table = good in that suit) if playing with conventions. Discard low cards on opponent point tricks.
strategy.advanced: La Politaine is riskyâ€”you may not get the lead or may be forced to break the sequence. Some variants require leading the Ace first when playing La Politaine to guarantee at least one point in the first trick. Coordinate with partner to establish leads.
tips: If holding La Politaine, announce before playing the first card.
Leading the Ace first from a Politaine guarantees the first trick is worth at least 1 point.
Watch for four 7sâ€”they win the game before play begins.

variations.name: Capot
variations.description: A team that wins all 8 tricks wins the whole game immediately.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes win condition to capot; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Four 8s
variations.description: Player dealt all four 8s declares before the first lead; that team wins the game. Replaces or supplements four 7s rule.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant swaps four 8s for four 7s instant win; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Target 32
variations.description: Game ends at 32 points. If both reach 32 in the same deal, first to claim wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes target score to 32; add engine.constants or scoring overrides when implemented.

variations.name: Long Game
variations.description: Play to 200 points for a longer session.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes target score to 200; add scoring overrides when implemented.

variations.name: Signals
variations.description: Tap table = good cards in led suit; slide card = good in same-color suit. Used to signal partner.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Convention only; no change to engine rules or phases.

variations.name: Redeal
variations.description: Hand with no 10s, 9s, or Aces may demand a redeal before first lead.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds optional redeal rule; no engine overrides documented in sources.

variations.name: Pollack
variations.description: German variant; declarations (Pollack 10-9-A, four of a kind, triplets) score before play; game to 21. No four-7s win.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Separate game with different scoring and declarations; overrides not yet mapped.

scoring.description: Point-trick scoring. Aces 1 each; 10, 9, K, Q, J 1/3 each; 8 and 7 no value; last trick 1. La Politaine bonus 11. Total 11 points per hand (fractions ignored).
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 31 or more points wins. Four sevens in hand wins immediately. Tie at 33: another deal to decide.

synthesis.shortDescription: French-Canadian no-trump trick game: collect points, score La Politaine, or hold four 7s to win.

hero.title: QUATRE SEPT

hero.tagline: Four sevens win the game. La Politaine wins the points.
